items.title: Somali families face renewed violence amid worsening hunger crisis
items.description: A health facility has also been damaged, according to the UN Children's Fund, UNICEF, and other humanitarian agencies. In the past few weeks, clashes have broken out in Baidoa, the state's largest city, between Government forces and fighters loyal to the former regional president, who was ousted in March. The army has been seeking to maintain control of the city, which it seized earlier this year. items.title: Hunger and malnutrition crises persist in Somalia as projected floods and funding shortfalls threaten vulnerable populations
items.description: The Federal Government of Somalia and the United Nations warn that projected flooding and funding shortfalls could worsen the hunger crisis and push more people – especially children -- into extreme food insecurity and acute malnutrition.   The latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)* analysis projects that 5.4 million people will face crisis levels of hunger or worse between October and December 2026, including 1.5 million people facing emergency levels of hunger or worse. items.titleIt: Hunger and malnutrition crises persist in Somalia as projected floods and funding shortfalls threaten vulnerable populations

items.title: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough
items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. Aadan Rooble knows the pattern well. He walked for part of the ten days it took him to reach Mogadishu after airstrikes made the decision for him — the farm his family worked in the village of Farxaano was no longer somewhere anyone could stay. His sons now find casual work when they can. He doesn't expect to go home. He's one of tens of thousands of farmers who have fled Somalia's Lower Shabelle region over the past decade, arriving in M
items.titleIt: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud
items.titleIt: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany

items.title: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57
items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The late Qoyste was a veteran journalist and one of the most remarkable radio journalists in Somalia, known for his distinctive and memorable voice. He first worked as an archive manager at the Ministry of Labour of the Somali central government in the 1980s before joining the print media in Mogadishu in the early 1990s, as the country descended into civil war. Qoyste became involved in journalism after his family moved from Beledweyne in c
items.titleIt: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57

items.description: The multilateral missions that have helped the Somali government fight Al-Shabaab for nearly two decades may be coming to an end. Mogadishu and its partners should get started now developing a plan for what they will do next.

items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. items.description: [Agenzia Fides] Adigrat -- "It is extremely urgent to facilitate humanitarian access, dialogue for peace and every form of dialogue. items.description: (ANSA) - ROMA, 29 SET - The 54th edition of the Africa Concours d’Elegance took place in Nairobi. Organized by the Alfa Romeo Owners Club (Kenya) since 1971, the event is the most prestigious and eagerly anticipated gathering on the continental African motorsports calendar dedicated to classic cars and motorcycles. The Ngong Racetrack hosted the classic Alfa Romeos with which the Italian Embassy, together with the Italian Cultural Institute in Nairobi and the ICE Agency, celebrated the design, engineering, and creativity that define Italian excellence. items.title: AU, U.S. Call for De-escalation as Tensions Rise in Tigray
items.description: African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf expressed concern over reports that Tigray forces had seized the airports in Mekelle, Axum and Shire, detained federal personnel and disrupted civilian air services. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to the three destinations on Wednesday, citing the "current situation" in the region, according to Addis Standard. The airline said passengers would be notified when services resume. items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud
items.titleIt: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany

items.title: Somali Journalist Mohamed Aweys Moodey Dies After Stabbing in Germany
items.description: The incident reportedly occurred at a residential facility. German authorities have identified a 28-year-old Somali man as the suspect. Police and prosecutors are investigating the circumstances of the incident, including the motive and whether it was connected to an earlier dispute between the two men. Moodey was a veteran journalist who worked in Somali media for many years. In 2014, he was arrested in Ethiopia and later sentenced to 27 years in prison under the country's anti-terrorism laws.
